The staple became the poster child for inflation, at one point becoming more expensive than beef. This year has been a different story, with prices plunging as egg producers overbuilt their laying flocks, preparing for more severe bird flu outbreaks that weren’t realized. items.text: What Is A Digital Arrest Scam? A Three-Month Case Shows How Fraudsters Trap Victims
items.article: Scammers posing as police and TRAI officials kept a Gujarat victim under "digital arrest" for three months. Here is how the scam works and how to spot it. A recent case from Gujarat shows how far “digital arrest" scams can go. Cybercriminals posing as police officers and officials of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) allegedly kept a victim under “digital arrest" for about three months and coerced him into transferring Rs. 11.42 crore to accounts they controlled. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has since arrested two more people in the case after searches at 22 locations across 10 states. The CBI alleges the two used a private company’s bank account to receive Rs. 2.5 crore of the money and moved it onward to other accounts to hide the trail. In a digital arrest scam, fraudsters pretend to be police, investigators or government officials, usually over phone and video calls. They tell victims they are involved in a serious crime and must stay on camera or remain in contact while an “investigation" is carried out. Victims are kept isolated, threatened with immediate arrest and pressured into transferring money, often described as a security deposit or a step to “clear their name." Scammers often begin by claiming to be from TRAI or a telecom company, warning that the victim’s mobile number is linked to illegal activity and will be disconnected.
